skills_considered.reason: A complete local PMC XML was already present; retrieval was limited to a visual PDF after standalone image routes failed.
The operator fixed the sequential paper list, so reprioritisation could not alter the cursor.
Canonical ledgers are BATCH_COMMIT-only; findings land in a dossier and commit candidate.
This review maps models and exposes a citation error but does not justify a new therapeutic hypothesis.
No intervention, dose, safety experiment or treatment window is tested.
BLOCK_BATCH_COMMIT remains explicit and no canonical scientific current file was edited.

group_assessment.weighting: The Aqeilan group is a high-volume primary WWOX laboratory and authored several models synthesized here. That improves model-context knowledge but creates same-group dependence. The paper is weighted as informed synthesis, not independent replication, and every experimental result remains attached to its cited primary.

field_density.note: Broad full-text intersections are dense and include secondary mentions. This review is useful as a historical atlas, but density does not repair species attribution or convert cited work into independent evidence.

multihop.note: All 111 references were read sequentially. Reference 53 is the human Mallaret SCAR12 paper, not a mouse seizure experiment; reference 104 is the rat lde/lde seizure paper PMID 19500159. The listed load-bearing WWOX sources resolve in the local registry or read queue; this review inherits none of their DATO status.

corpus_crossquery.query: How does the 2018 animal-model atlas compare with Steinberg 2021, and does its mouse-seizure statement survive the completed primary citation chain?
corpus_crossquery.note: Post-reading audit found CORPUS-STUB-011, FT-047, the Steinberg 2021 dossier, PMID 19500159, PMID 19936220, CLAIM 005 and the existing dismissal record for the mouse-epilepsy attribution. The review predates cell-targeted CNS models and propagates a species/source error rather than repairing it.

retraction_check.result: The corrected comma-separated repository retraction check returned no retraction, expression of concern or correction for PMID 30370248 on 2026-08-10.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: The fingerprinted local JATS artifact identifies PMCID PMC6194312, PMID 30370248 and DOI 10.3389/fonc.2018.00420; it contains a complete body, one figure, one table and 111 references.

entries.proposition: The review calls the mineralisation-stage osteoblast defect cell-autonomous.
entries.snippet: This delay in bone formation was the result of cell–autonomous defect in osteoblast differentiation beginning at the mineralisation stage.
entries.anchor: Bone phenotype of Wwox null mice, paragraph 1

entries.proposition: The hypomorph-survival mechanism is explicitly presumed rather than tested.
entries.snippet: This increased viability phenotype was presumed to be a result of low expression of WWOX in some tissues, which might have been sufficient for postnatal survival of Wwoxgt/gt mice

entries.proposition: The authors acknowledge unresolved phenotyping inconsistencies among conditional models.
entries.snippet: Nevertheless, there have been also some inconsistencies in phenotyping these models that shall be further investigated in future studies.

entries.proposition: Several mammary-specific Wwox-deletion models had developmental defects without mammary tumours.
entries.snippet: Surprisingly, none of these models developed mammary tumors
entries.anchor: Conditional Wwox ablation in mammary tissue, paragraph 1

entries.proposition: The review itself names cell of origin, cooperating changes and genetic background as determinants of tumour outcome.
entries.snippet: it depends on various factors, among which is dependency on cell of origin, combination with other genetic changes or even genetic background of the mouse model utilized
entries.anchor: Conditional Wwox ablation in mammary tissue, paragraph 1

entries.proposition: The body misattributes spontaneous and audiogenic seizures to a Wwox-KO mouse and to Mallaret reference 53.
entries.snippet: Mallaret et al. showed that the short–lived Wwox KO mouse displays spontaneous and audiogenic seizures (53).
entries.anchor: Significance of WWOX in neurological disorders, paragraph 2

entries.proposition: Reference 53 is a human recessive cerebellar-ataxia paper, not a mouse seizure experiment.
entries.snippet: The tumour suppressor gene WWOX is mutated in autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia with epilepsy and mental retardation.

entries.proposition: The actual spontaneous-mutation animal seizure citation in this review is a rat study.
entries.snippet: A spontaneous mutation of the Wwox gene and audiogenic seizures in rats with lethal dwarfism and epilepsy.

entries.proposition: The review acknowledges that phenotypes differ between mouse and rat models.
entries.snippet: some of the phenotypes reported in the mouse models were not reported or observed in the rat model. This could be related to the approach used in genetic manipulation and/or genetic background.

entries.proposition: The review records that a reported fly irradiation phenotype was caused by a background insertion.
entries.snippet: Later on, it was reported that background mutation as a result of insertion of piggyBag transposon into the second intron of DmWwox was responsible for this phenotype.

entries.proposition: Figure 1 visually compresses mouse and rat phenotypes into one rodent category.
entries.snippet: The single box labelled Rodents lists post-natal lethality, metabolic defects, tumour phenotypes and 'Seizures, epilepsy, & ataxia' without species, genotype, strain, age or assay separation.
